title: How the Recall Paid-Month Credit Is Figured, TRICARE Retired Reserve
content:
For a TRICARE Retired Reserve plan under the TRICARE Premium-Based Plans, the recall paid-month credit is figured as the days of the most recently paid month after the plan's termination date, multiplied by the amount billed for that month divided by the days its bill covers, with nothing taken off or added for coverage-type changes, rounded to the cent once at the end.

## Inputs and where they are read

| Input | Read from |
|---|---|
| Most recently paid month | the coverage month of the bill settled by the latest posted premium payment on the plan |
| Amount billed and days covered | that bill, as the premium ledger shows it |
| Whether a later month has been billed | the plan's monthly bill with the latest due date; the credit is figured only where that is a later month than the most recently paid month, and is 0.00 otherwise |
| Plan's termination date | the plan record; with none recorded no day of the month comes after it, and the credit is 0.00 |

The days after the termination date run from the day following it through the last day of the month. The figure is rounded to the cent once, at the end, and is never less than zero.

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

A TRICARE Retired Reserve Member-Only plan, monthly bill for May of 614.07 covering 31 days and paid; the June bill already posted; termination date 19 May. Days after the termination date: 20 to 31 May, 12 days. Credit: 12 multiplied by 614.07, divided by 31, is 237.7045, rounded once to 237.70.
